text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 0.75 to each of 4 members, so 3 total per token—socially efficient since 3 exceeds the cost of 1. But individually, keeping a token nets 1 versus only 0.75 from contributing, so the dominant strategy is to free-ride and contribute nothing, even though full cooperation would be best for the group.

Given it's a repeated 10-round game, I'll open with a moderate signal of cooperation rather than full defection—contributing 10 seems like a reasonable starting move to test the group's willingness to cooperate.
